input: # A trailing decimal point with an exponent is a DecimalLiteral, but the
# integer part still may not carry a leading zero.
# An exponent that overflows the double range is Infinity in ECMAScript,
# not a parse error, and not unquoted text. Both runtimes must agree.
# A hexadecimal literal wider than the exact double integer range has to be
# rounded ONCE from the exact integer, the way ECMAScript parseInt does it.
# A digit-by-digit floating-point fold rounds at every digit and lands one
# unit in the last place low, which is altered data rather than a different
# spelling of the same number. Both prefix spellings, and a negative.
# Exactly half way, so the tie goes to the even mantissa: 2^53+1 is 2^53.
